searchText: Note that, since a field element is slightly under 255 bits wide (that is, it doesn't quite fill 32 bytes), the amount of data that can be encoded into a blob is a little less than 128KiB in practice - that may be what the 125KiB relates to. I don't see how? ``` >>> floor(log2(52435875175126190479447740508185965837690552500527637822603658699938581184513)) 254 ``` isn't enough to account for that I'm guessing relating to ``` >>> 128/1024 0.125 ``` interesting coincidence How can two rollups share a single blob together? Is it as simple as: - rollup a sends a 50kb blob into the mempool - rollup b sends a 50kb blob into the mempool The builder sees this and bundles both blob transactions into a a single blob, pads the remaining (~28kb) with zeros, and then sends this blob execution payload header to the validator? <dankrad> No, it does not work like that. THey would have to coordinate to create a single transaction with a combined blob

excerpts.author: 0xevan
excerpts.content:
How can two rollups share a single blob together? Is it as simple as:
- rollup a sends a 50kb blob into the mempool
- rollup b sends a 50kb blob into the mempool

The builder sees this and bundles both blob transactions into a a single blob,  pads the remaining (~28kb) with zeros, and then sends this blob execution payload header to the validator?
